summary.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q2 FY27 call: management targets 5-7% FY27 like-for-like growth, with Domino's price hikes of 140-200 bps offsetting dairy, chicken and vegetable inflation.
summary.overview: The transcript is a Q&A-only call with no prepared financial figures read out; the shareholder letter was referenced but not reproduced. Management said Domino's like-for-like growth is planned at 5-7% for the full year, with Q3 tracking to plan and the festive period cited as a swing factor of 100-200 bps. Price increases of about 140-200 bps have been taken selectively, and management said it will take further price if needed. Popeyes is described as the second growth engine, but restaurant-level unit economics still need work, with gross margin upside of 100-200 bps and store-level profitability dependent on higher average daily sales (target about Rs 1 lakh per day). Turkey (Turkish operations) reported LFL is negative due to accounting for inflation, which management says masks positive transaction growth.

financial_highlights.change: Calibrated via machine-learning models, not blunt increases
Management says Q4 to Q1 to Q2 shows an uptick; Q3 planned within range

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin absorption of unplanned cost
financial_highlights.value: About 140 bps absorbed of 200 bps unplanned cost

financial_highlights.metric: Popeyes gross margin improvement still available
financial_highlights.change: Management cites 200 bps as further opportunity in one answer
Early read: adds material to ADS, mostly dining
Next 150 stores planned, taking network towards Rs 1,000 crore run-rate

financial_highlights.value: About 400 stores targeted; around 100 done (per question), about three quarters to complete

segments.name: Domino's India
segments.commentary: Average order growth per store is positive and price increases are running ahead of company cost inflation, but LFL is reported negative for Domino's Turkey-related accounting. Dine-in and takeaway is a stated headwind that management wants turned to at least +1-2% to LFL.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: About 100 stores in 25 cities; management says it has established a second growth engine, but restaurant-level profitability is not yet in place. Gross margin benefits from Domino's supply-chain scale; store rentals are higher than Domino's legacy sites.

segments.name: Hong's/Homs (Hong's Kitchen? brand as referenced)
segments.commentary: Management says drag from emerging brands is ahead of plan, with about 100 bps of margin benefit already delivered. Brand name in transcript is unclear and should be verified.

segments.name: Domino's Cafe
segments.commentary: About 15-20 stores; early read is positive for average daily sales, with payback and customer profile still under review.

guidance_outlook: Domino's FY27 LFL guidance of 5-7%, with Q3 tracking to plan; festive weeks could move numbers by 100-200 bps.
Gross margin: another 100-200 bps of improvement cited for Domino's and about 200 bps for Popeyes.
Popeyes: about 40-45 openings guided per year, with 150 further sites identified; accelerating only as backend supply chain and quality permit.
Management aims to lift Popeyes average daily sales toward Rs 1 lakh per day to improve store margins.
Management said it would take further price increases if inflation persists.
capex_capacity: Domino's refurbishment programme covering about 400 stores, with about three quarters to complete.
Popeyes: about 100 stores; next 150 sites mapped geography by geography, with expansion gated by supply-chain build.
Co-located Domino's and Popeyes food-court style formats in a few high-street sites; management says it is opportunistic and not a scaled programme yet.
demand_pricing: Cheese: management says the company is covered for FY27 on cheese supplies, but dairy inflation is passing through with a timing lag; chicken and vegetables also seeing inflation (monsoon and West Asia crisis cited).
Demand: management says the business is about 100% urban and does not see rural weakness; it sees pressure mainly as inflation rather than demand.
Competition: coffee pricing was previously too high for Turkey value positioning, and management says it has corrected this and is targeting younger consumers near universities.

qa_highlights.question: How much more price can be taken given dairy and cheese inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has taken about 140-200 bps of price so far via calibrated models; cheese is covered for FY27, and further price increases are possible if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5-7% LFL a full-year number, and what is the second-half trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is for a full-year 5-7% range, with Q3 on track and an uptick seen from Q4 through Q2; festive weeks could shift the numbers by 100-200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MAU growing about 25% while MTU grows only about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said online delivery is under-penetrated and new customers are being acquired through revamped digital marketing; conversion is lower for first-time users, but long-term customer value is not seen declining.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress and timeline on store refurbishment and the beta channel?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 stores are being refurbished, roughly 100 done so far, with about three quarters to complete; this quarter was the first in which overall revenue grew.

qa_highlights.question: Can Popeyes accelerate, and what is the path to store profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance remains about 40-45 openings a year, constrained by real estate and supply-chain build; store profitability depends on ADS approaching Rs 1 lakh per day and on 100-200 bps of gross margin upside.

qa_highlights.question: How much did innovation contribute to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose the contribution directly, but says innovation over the last year contributes almost double-digit percentage points to top-line growth, led by chicken, cheese and beverage platforms.

risks_watch: Dairy, chicken and vegetable inflation, plus LPG and wage pressure; management says about 60 bps of unplanned cost remains unabsorbed.
Festive-season demand (next 7-10 days and Christmas period) could move LFL by 100-200 bps.
Dine-in and takeaway remain a headwind to LFL; management wants this to turn positive.
Popeyes store economics: rentals are higher than Domino's legacy sites and store-level margin depends on ADS scaling.
Turkey: reported LFL negative due to inflation accounting; management offered limited operating disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Domino's trajectory and gross-margin levers, but cautious and non-committal on near-term numbers (declining to raise expectations). Candid that Popeyes unit economics are not yet proven, and open about the Turkey LFL accounting drag.
key_quotes: So we have taken about 140 or 150 to 200 basis point of price increases, very calibrated through machine learning models versus taking blunt price increases, where we can depart channels.
I think we've planned it to have a full year in the 5 to 7% range.
We believe we have established the second growth engine for jubilant food works, built on product differentiation, service differentiation and customer loss.

adds.what: Popeyes next 150 stores identified; mid-term opening guidance about 40-45 stores per year
Domino's Cafe: about 15-20 stores (early read positive for ADS)
Domino's store refurbishment of about 400 stores (~100 done, ~3 quarters to complete); refurbishment, not new capacity

growth.why: Management held Domino's FY27 like-for-like guidance at 5-7% (midpoint 6%), with Q3 tracking to plan, backed partly by 140-200 bps of price increases and about 140 bps of 200 bps cost inflation absorbed, plus Popeyes openings of about 40-45 per year with 150 sites identified but gated by supply chain.
